Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:46: Regarding the punishment for one who has relations with a maidservant, it says in Vayikra Rabbah (9:5), these are his words: another interpretation, "if he offers it for thanksgiving" (Leviticus 7:12) — this is what the verse says (Proverbs 14:9), "fools mock guilt." Rabbi Yudan said, this fool translates his guilt with his mouth and says, "I am not liable for a sin-offering nor for a guilt-offering." Rabbi Yudan in the name of Rabbi Levi said, these are people who treat maidservants as permitted in this world — the Holy One, blessed be He, will hang them by the crowns of their heads in the future to come, as it is said (Psalms 68:22), "but God will smite the head of His enemies, the hairy crown of one who walks about in his guilt." All the people shall say, that man was contemptible in his guilt. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:47: Further, they said in the great tractate Derech Eretz — found among us in manuscript, and copied in the Yalkut (portion Ki Tetze, §931): one who has relations with a maidservant is liable for fourteen prohibitions and karet at the hands of Heaven — because of "you shall not sow your vineyard with mixed seed," because of "you shall not plow [with mixed animals]," because of "you shall not wear shatnez," because of "you shall not murder," because of "you shall not commit adultery," because of "you shall not steal," because of "you shall not covet," and "you shall not testify [falsely]," and because of [the prohibition of relations with] one's father's wife, and because of one's brother's wife, because of a maidservant, because of a harlot, because of a niddah, because of a foreign woman. If he was an Israelite and profaned himself and his seed with a Cutheite [gentile] woman, he will have no "waking" one among the wise and no "answering" one among the students [i.e., no worthy descendants]; and if he was a priest, he will have no son to offer an offering to the LORD of Hosts. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:48: Further, they said in Sanhedrin (82a), on the verse (Malachi 2:11), "Judah has dealt treacherously, and an abomination has been done in Israel": Rav said, "Judah has dealt treacherously" refers to idolatry, as it says (Jeremiah 3:20), "you have dealt treacherously with Me, house of Israel, says the LORD." "And an abomination has been done in Israel" — this refers to lying with a male, as it says (Leviticus 18:22), "and you shall not lie with a male as with a woman; it is an abomination." "For Judah has profaned the holiness of the LORD, which He loved" — this refers to a harlot, as it says (Deuteronomy 23:18), "there shall be no cult-harlot among the children of Israel." "And has married the daughter of a foreign god" — this refers to one who has relations with a Cutheite woman. And it is written after it, "may the LORD cut off, for the man who does this, waking one and answering one" — if he is a Torah scholar, he will have no waking one among the wise and no answering one among the students; and if he is a priest, he will have no son to offer an offering to the LORD of Hosts. Rabbi Chiya bar Abuya said, whoever has relations with a Cutheite woman is as though he had married into idolatry, as it is said, "and has married the daughter of a foreign god." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:49: Further, in the Midrash on (Proverbs 5:3), "for the lips of a strange woman drip honey": my son, beware of a harlot woman, lest she deceive you with the matter of lips, and lest she lead you astray after her voice. Why? "But her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a double-edged sword" — he said to him, my son, just as a sword devours from both sides, so she destroys a person's life from the life of this world and from the life of the World to Come. What is written after it? "Her feet go down to death" — for she brings a person down to the depths of death, and this refers to evil suffering. "Her steps take hold of Sheol" — even though he is judged with suffering in this world, he is not saved from the judgment of Gehinnom. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:50: Regarding the punishment for one who has relations with another man's wife, or an unmarried woman without the seven blessings, it is explained in the Zohar (portion Tazria, 44b), these are his words: from here we learn that a bridegroom and bride, once blessed with the seven blessings, become attached as one, corresponding to the pattern above. Therefore, whoever comes to unite with another woman, he thereby blemishes the union — he creates, as it were, two domains above, for the union of the Community of Israel is with the Holy One, blessed be He, alone, whether at a time of mercy or at a time of judgment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:51: Come and see: whoever unites with another woman is as though he deals falsely with the Holy One, blessed be He, and with the Community of Israel; therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, does not grant him repentance — it depends on repentance only until he departs from this world. This is what is written (Isaiah 22:14), "surely this iniquity shall not be atoned for you until you die" — and when? At the time he enters into repentance in that world, and must accept his punishment [there].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:52: Rabbi Elazar said, this one who deals falsely with the Community of Israel will not be accepted in repentance until he is judged in the judgment of Gehinnom; all the more so one who deals falsely with the Community of Israel and with the Holy One, blessed be He, and all the more so if he troubles the Holy One, blessed be He, to create the form of an illegitimate child through another woman, and weakens the King's entourage.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:53: Rabbi Chiya opened and said, "one who robs his father and his mother" (Proverbs 28:24) — "his father" is the Holy One, blessed be He; "his mother" is the Community of Israel. What is "robs"? As it is said (Isaiah 3:14), "the plunder of the poor is in your houses" — and who is this? Whoever desires another woman who is not his true mate. We have learned there: whoever enjoys this world without a blessing is as though he robs the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Community of Israel, as it is written, "one who robs his father and his mother." "Whoever enjoys this world" — in general, this refers to one who attaches himself to a woman to enjoy her, even if she is unmarried and he enjoys her without a blessing — as though he robs the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Community of Israel. Why? Because their union is with seven blessings. And if this applies to an unmarried woman, how much more so one who attaches himself to another's wife, who stands in the pattern of the union above, with the seven blessings — all the more so. "He is a companion to a destroyer" — this is Jeroboam, as they have established; and it says "there is no transgression" [i.e., he says]: is she not unmarried, why is it forbidden? Because of this, "he robs his father and his mother," and moreover "he is a companion to a destroyer." Who is "a destroyer"? One who blemishes the pattern and correction above; all the more so one who desires his fellow's wife to attach himself to her, who blemishes even more, and is thereby blemished forever — "a man who destroys" — for he blemishes above, blemishes below, and blemishes his own soul. This is what is written, "a destroyer" — and it is written (Proverbs 6:32), "he who destroys his own soul does this."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:54: Regarding the punishment for relations with a Cutheite woman, it is explained in the Zohar (portion Chayei Sarah, 131): whoever attaches himself to a woman of the other nations, worshippers of idols, becomes impure himself, and the child born to him will receive upon himself a spirit of impurity. And should you say, but this comes from the side of his father [not the mother, who is not Jewish] — why should he receive a spirit of impurity? Come and see: for first his father became impure at the time he attached himself to that woman who is impure; and since he sinned by becoming impure through that impure woman, all the more so will the child born from her receive a spirit of impurity — and moreover, he has transgressed the Torah, as it is written (Exodus 34:14), "for you shall not bow to another god, for the LORD, whose name is jealous [Kanah]" — because He is jealous over this covenant. And he says below: come and see, this one who brings the holy covenant into that woman of the other nations causes himself to become impure and causes another place to become impure, and therefore it is written (Proverbs 30:21), "under three the earth trembles" [and this is the fourth]. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:55: Further, in the Zohar (portion Va'etchanan, 266a), while they were walking, Rabbi Abba said, what is the meaning of what is written (Jeremiah 2:13), "they have forsaken Me, the source of living waters, to hew for themselves cisterns, broken cisterns" etc.? "They have forsaken Me" — this refers to one who deals falsely with the holy marked sign [the covenant]. And in what does he deal falsely with it? That he brings it into another domain, called "broken cisterns" — for the nations of the world, worshippers of idols, are called "broken cisterns," while Israel is called a "well" from which clear waters flow forth and stream, as in (Song of Songs 4:15), "and streams from Lebanon," "and streams from your own well" (Proverbs 5:15), and it is written (Song of Songs 4:15), "a garden spring, a well of living waters." What is "which the waters cannot contain"? Rather, that river which flows and issues waters all the garden and moistens every single place, as we have established, until it fills that garden-place called "a well of living waters," and from there the supernal and lower beings are nourished, as in (Genesis 2:10), "and from there it divides." And all those sides on the side of the left are not watered from that spring of waters that flows, since they are from the side of the other nations; and whoever deals falsely with the holy Name on that side attaches himself to "broken cisterns which the waters cannot contain," and they did not enter there [the true well]. But one who merits to guard it merits to be watered from that flow of the river, in this world and in the World to Come — this is what is written (Jeremiah 58:11 [Isaiah 58:11]), "and you shall be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water whose waters do not fail" — and he merits that that supernal well fills up, to draw blessings above and below. Woe to one who deals falsely with the holy Name, for he deals falsely with the supernal Name, and moreover causes this well not to be blessed — of him we read (Deuteronomy 22:19), "for he has brought forth an evil name against a virgin of Israel" — precisely "a virgin of Israel." Thus far his words, as relevant to our purpose.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:56: Regarding the punishment for one who has relations with a niddah, a maidservant, a foreign woman, or a harlot, it says in Tikkunim (59b), these are his words: and all the adhesions of the deadly poison are her feet, of which it is said (Proverbs 5:5), "her feet go down to death" — these are the eighteen adhesions, of which it is written (Genesis 8:21), "and I will never again smite every living thing as I have done" — [corresponding] to those eighteen blessings of the prayers. And who causes the waters of the Flood to increase? Whoever pours out the waters of the seed of the covenant of circumcision into a niddah, a maidservant, a Cutheite woman, or a harlot. And an animal with a fatal wound [treifah] never lives — for wherever a person becomes attached through his sins, he kills. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:57: Further, in Tikkunim (78b): there are three kelipot of the foreskin [orlah], and they are: destroyer, anger, and wrath — corresponding to "orlah" [foreskin] is the sin, for which they established in the prayer, "and He, being merciful, forgives iniquity, and does not destroy" — this is "destroyer"; "and abundantly turns away His anger" — this is "anger"; "and does not stir up all His wrath" — this is "wrath." And whoever brings the sign of the covenant into a foreign domain, these four rule over him; this is what is written (Genesis 7:19), "and the waters prevailed very, very greatly upon the earth" — "upon the earth" refers to his own body. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:58: Further, in Tikkunim (85a), this sin mentioned is truly comparable to one who blemishes the Shabbat by carrying from a private domain to a public domain. These are his words: whoever uproots an object from its place and puts it down outside its place is as though he uprooted the Tree of Life, which is the covenant, and put it down in a foreign domain. Whoever does this causes his soul to be uprooted from its own domain and put down in another domain, which is gall and spleen; and this caused Israel to be uprooted from the land of Israel and exiled into a foreign land, which is a public domain. And so it is with whoever brings his holy sign of the covenant into a foreign domain. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:59: Further, in Tikkunim (there, 97b): likewise, whoever goes out from a private domain into a public domain, or emits seed from the sign of the holy covenant and brings it into a foreign domain, is as though he plants the tree of good and evil; therefore this person who plants in a niddah, a maidservant, a Cutheite woman, or a harlot — of him it is said (Exodus 20:4), "you shall not make for yourself a graven image or any likeness" — and regarding the daughter born in this manner, she is called "a molten image" [masekhah], and of them it is said (Deuteronomy 27:15), "cursed be the man who makes a graven or molten image" etc. "and sets it up in secret" — what is "in secret"? In the secret of the world. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:60: Further, regarding the punishment for relations with a Cutheite woman and with a niddah, in the Zohar (portion Shemot, 3a), these are his words: there are three who push the Shechinah from the world, and cause the dwelling of the Holy One, blessed be He, not to be in the world; and people cry out and their voice is not heard — and these are they: one who lies with a niddah, since there is no impurity as severe in the world as the impurity of a niddah — the impurity of a niddah is harsher than all other impurities of the world; he becomes impure, and everyone who comes near him becomes impure with him, and wherever they go the Shechinah is pushed away before them. Moreover, this causes evil illnesses upon himself and upon the child he begets — for once a person approaches that impurity that hovers over her and becomes impure in all his limbs, the seed he begets at that time draws upon it a spirit of impurity, and all his days he will be in impurity, since his very structure and foundation is a greater and more severe impurity than all other impurities in the world — for the moment a person approaches a niddah, that impurity hovering over her [attaches to him], as it is written (Leviticus 15:24), "and her impurity shall be upon him."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:61: And whoever lies with "the daughter of a foreign god," bringing the holy covenant and the sign of the covenant into another domain, as it is written (Malachi 2:11), "and has married the daughter of a foreign god" — and we have learned, there is no jealousy before the Holy One, blessed be He, except the jealousy of the holy covenant, which is the sign of the holy Name and the secret of faith. What is written? (Numbers 25:1), "and the people began to whore after the daughters of Moab" — immediately, "and the LORD's anger burned against Israel." The heads of the people, who knew and did not protest against them, were punished first, as it is written (ibid. 25:4), "take all the heads of the people and hang them before the LORD, facing the sun." Rabbi Abba said, what is "facing the sun" [nagged hashemesh]? Facing the covenant, which is called "sun," of which it is said (Psalms 84:12), "for the LORD God is a sun and a shield" — "sun and shield" is the holy covenant. Just as the sun rises and illuminates the world, so the holy covenant rises and illuminates a person's body. "A shield" — just as a shield protects a person, so the holy covenant shields a person; and one who guards it, no harm in the world can approach him. This is "facing the sun." The heads of the people will be seized in every single generation for this sin, if they know [of it and do nothing], since this sin is upon them, to arouse the jealousy of the Holy One, blessed be He, over this covenant.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:62: Whoever brings this holiness into another domain — of him it is written (Exodus 20:3), "you shall have no other gods before Me; you shall not bow down to them nor serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God" — and it is all one jealousy; therefore the Shechinah is pushed away before him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:63: Whoever deals falsely with the holy covenant sealed in a person's flesh is as though he deals falsely with the holy Name, blessed be He; whoever deals falsely with the King's seal deals falsely with the King himself; he has no portion in the God of Israel unless he continually [engages in] the power of repentance.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:64: Rabbi Yosi opened and said, "and the children of Israel forsook the LORD, and He sold them" etc. What is "forsook"? That they pushed away from themselves the holy covenant [sign]; they would circumcise but not uncover [peri'ah], until Deborah came and made this obligatory for all Israel, as it is written (Judges 5:2), "when the leaders led in Israel, when the people volunteered themselves, bless the LORD" [interpreting "befarah pera'ot" as related to peri'ah].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:65: Whoever kills his own children — this refers to one whose wife becomes pregnant and he causes her to lose the child in her womb, since he tears down the building of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His workmanship. There is one who kills a [born] person, but this one kills his own children. He does three evils that the whole world cannot bear, and therefore the world melts away little by little without being known, and the Holy One, blessed be He, departs from the world, and sword, famine, and plague come upon the world. And these are they: [1] he kills his children; [2] he destroys the King's building, pushing away the soul that goes wandering in the world and finds no rest, and therefore the spirit of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it were, weeps, and the world is judged with all these judgments — woe to that person, woe to him, it would have been better for him not to have been created in the world. Fortunate is Israel, who, even while in the exile of Egypt, guarded themselves from all these three. Thus far his words, as relevant to our purpose.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:66: Regarding what is said (Psalms 45:4), "gird your sword upon your thigh, mighty one" — according to the first interpretation, this means that the sword that avenges the vengeance of the covenant is what exacts payment from one who blemishes the covenant. Rashbi, peace be upon him, likewise explained this at length (Zohar, portion Vaera, 26a), these are his words: Rabbi Shimon opened and said (Job 19:29), "be afraid of the sword, for wrath brings the punishments of the sword, that you may know there is judgment" — [reading] "shadin" [judgment/demons] is written [suggesting a double meaning]. "Be afraid of the sword" — which sword? This sword that avenges the vengeance of the covenant — for this sword stands to observe whoever deals falsely with the covenant, for whoever deals falsely with the covenant, this sword is the vengeance exacted from him, as it is written, "for wrath brings the punishments of the sword." Why? Because whoever deals falsely with the covenant separates desire, and does not guard what should be guarded, and does not give to its [proper] place, since he does not arouse [it] toward its [proper] place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:67: And whoever guards this covenant causes this covenant to be aroused toward its [proper] place, and the supernal and lower beings are blessed. Who arouses this covenant toward its place? When the righteous are found in the world. From where do we learn this? From here: (Exodus 6:4), "and I have also established My covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings [megureihem] in which they sojourned [garu]." What is "their sojournings"? As in "be afraid [giru] of the sword" — since it is a place where sojourning/fear rests in the world; therefore "be afraid of the sword." "In which they sojourned" — from the day they drew near to the Holy One, blessed be He, they cast a fear upon it — a supernal fear, to guard His commandments; for if he does not cast this fear upon his own head, he will never fear the Holy One, blessed be He. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:68: Further, regarding the merit of one who guards the sign of the covenant, and the punishment of one who blemishes it, it is explained in the Zohar (portion Lech Lecha, 94a), these are his words: he opened another [discourse] and said, "had not the LORD been my help, my soul would soon have dwelt in silence [Dumah]" (Psalms 94:17). We have learned: by what do Israel merit not to go down to Gehinnom and not to be handed into the hand of Dumah [the angel of the grave]? Through this sign — for so we have learned, at the time a person departs from the world, several groups of pure ones are appointed over him; they lift their eyes and see this sign, which is the mark of holiness, and separate from him, and he is not given into the hand of Dumah below to Gehinnom — for whoever is handed over into his hand certainly descends to Gehinnom. From this sign supernal and lower beings fear, and evil judgments do not rule over a person if he merits guarding this sign, since it is bound to the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He. Since King David did not guard this sign of the covenant as fitting, the kingdom was taken from him and he was driven out of Jerusalem; immediately he feared and thought that he would be handed to Dumah and would die in that world, until it was told to him, as it is written (2 Samuel 12:13), "the LORD has also removed your sin; you shall not die." At that moment he opened and said, "had not the LORD been my help, my soul would soon have dwelt in silence." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:69: The merit of one who guards the covenant is thus explained, as is his punishment — for it says that because he did not guard the sign of the covenant as befitting, he thought he would be handed over to Dumah, were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, was his guardian and advocate, as is explained in the Zohar (portion Bereshit, 8b). And if David feared Dumah even though the matter had been permitted — for whoever went to a war of the house of David would write a bill of divorce for his wife [beforehand] (ibid.; Shabbat 56a) — nevertheless, since he did not guard the sign of the covenant properly, his Torah did not suffice to protect him from suffering. And our Sages of blessed memory said (Sanhedrin 93b) that King David, peace be upon him, was the head of the Sanhedrin and the halakhah followed him in every matter, as it is said (1 Samuel 16:18), "and skilled in speech," [meaning] that the halakhah followed him everywhere — one who blemished it without any doubt, who could be his advocate? Surely he would certainly be handed over to Dumah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:70: Behold, we find that despite all this David accepted mortification and suffering through fasts, as it is said (Psalms 109:24), "my knees are weak from fasting." And was it not that his being driven from his kingdom appeared to be because of his sin with Uriah, whom he had killed by the sword of the children of Ammon — as is said there in portion Bereshit? But regarding the sin with Bathsheba ["Uriah's wife"], the punishment was written concerning it, and he accepted it — and "the punishment was written" refers to what Nathan the prophet told him (2 Samuel 12:11), "behold, I will raise up evil against you from your own house." One who has sinned in the covenant, how much he must suffer through mortification and fasting all his days, as David did.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:71: And should someone say that Torah atones for sin — was not King David, peace be upon him, occupied with Torah more than we are, as they explained, and the Holy Spirit was upon him — why did he mortify himself in vain and not rely on his occupation with Torah day and night to atone for his sin? Rather, certainly what they said, that Torah atones, is along the lines of what the pious Rabbeinu Yonah, peace be upon him, explained in Sha'arei Teshuvah (Gate 1, §47), regarding what our Sages of blessed memory said (Rosh Hashanah 18a), that one who occupies himself with acts of loving-kindness has his sins atoned — meaning that his sufferings are suspended until he repents; so too one who occupies himself with Torah, the atonement is that his sufferings are postponed until he repents. But certainly he must purify himself from his sins through mortifications and fasts so that his Torah be acceptable, as we elaborated in the Gate of Repentance (ch. 3). Especially one who has sinned in the covenant, whose blemish is equivalent to the entire Torah — from the merits our Sages of blessed memory attributed to it, we know the greatness of the punishment for blemishing it, and they elaborated on its merit at length.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:72: In Tikkunim (65) it is also explained regarding the merit of one who guards the covenant, of whom it is said (Deuteronomy 28:10), "and all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of the LORD is called upon you" — for YHVH is marked in the covenant, as it is said (Deuteronomy 30:12), "*Mi *ya'aleh *lanu *hashamaymah" ["who shall go up for us to heaven"], whose initial letters spell "Milah" [circumcision] and final letters spell YHVH; and all accusers fear him. And he further says at the end of 64: therefore whoever guards the covenant of circumcision, which is his seal, death, that is, Satan, the evil inclination, impurity, the hidden one [Tzafoni], the angel of death, moves away from him, does not come near him, and does not cause him to die by its hand.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:73: Whoever deals falsely with the covenant of circumcision deals falsely with the King's seal, which is marked with Shaddai on the outside and YHVH within. From where do we learn this? From this verse, indicated by (Deuteronomy 30:12), "*Mi *ya'aleh *lanu *hashamaymah" — initial letters "Milah," final letters YHVH; and certainly whoever deals falsely with the covenant of circumcision has YHVH and Shaddai removed from him, and Satan rests upon him, who is "another god" — the serpent rests in the place where YHVH was within, and the deadly poison rests in the place where Shaddai was without. This is what the verse means (Numbers 19:20), "he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD" — if he does not return in repentance and bear several sufferings to remove that serpent from there and its deadly poison, which is a malignant leprosy through several illnesses and afflictions, until no flesh remains upon him — that is, dust; and the secret of the matter (Leviticus 14:42), "and he shall take other earth [dust] and plaster the house" — since "the serpent's food is dust" (Isaiah 65:25), until it is fed from that flesh it will not move from him. And a poor man is considered as dead — just as a corpse's face changes, so a poor man's face changes; and this has already been established (Berachot 6b), "like a chameleon [koram] to men" (Psalms 12:9) — what is "koram"? Whoever needs the help of others, his face changes like a chameleon, and how many bites of suffering that serpent bites him! Moreover, a poor man is considered like a metzora [afflicted with tzara'at] — just as a metzora, "his head shall be unshorn" etc. (Leviticus 13:45), so a poor man; just as a metzora "shall dwell outside the camp" (ibid. 13:46), so a poor man is naked and barefoot. And poverty is for Israel in the place of tzara'at.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:74: And he further says below: and if he returns in repentance, the elixir of life descends upon him, which is the Shechinah, of whom it is said (Isaiah 6:10), "and he shall return and be healed" from these kinds of illnesses, and heals him from the death of poverty, as in (Ezekiel 18:32), "return and live" — for Israel, when they are poor, are called dead, and regarding them it is said, "return and live." And there is no poverty like the poverty of Torah — whoever has no Torah is called dead; his healing for that world is what? Torah, of which it is said (Proverbs 3:18), "she is a tree of life to those who grasp her," and she is the healing for all illnesses, as in (ibid. 3:8), "it shall be healing to your navel" etc. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:75: From this statement it is understood that one who blemishes the covenant must suffer harsh afflictions close to death until that flesh in which the sin is marked is consumed. And especially if he blemished it through emitting seed in vain, which incurs the death penalty (Niddah 13a), he must accept upon himself sufferings close to death. The reason is that the blemish in it is great and comprehensive, since it touches the very essence of the Name YHVH, encompassing the positive and negative commandments — "shemi" [My name] with yod-heh equals 365, "zechari" [My remembrance] with vav-heh equals 248 (Tikkunei Zohar there, 64a) — and thus in blemishing the covenant he blemishes all positive and negative commandments, and requires suffering as though he had transgressed all of them individually.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:76: My teacher, peace be upon him, elaborated further on this, being precise about the wording of the statement that says, "and the secret of the matter, 'and he shall take other earth and plaster the house'" — this verse is explained in Tikkunim (102b-103a) regarding reincarnation [gilgul]. Now, regarding the acceptance of sufferings for repentance, it is comparable to one who is reincarnated: just as the reincarnated soul needs another building, since the first body was a dwelling for the external force and needs its dissolution, so in returning in repentance, one consumes the flesh that grew through the external force by mortifications and fasts.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:77: Rashbi, peace be upon him, needed to further bring the matter of "a poor man is considered as dead," to explain that he becomes comparable to the reincarnated soul in all his aspects — just as the poor man's face is greenish, this bears the reason of death, whose face is greenish, and "how many bites of suffering bite him," since the bones and flesh both need correction in the reincarnated soul, since the external force ruled over both — as we said above, that YHVH and Shaddai were removed from him and Samael, who is "another god," and his female, rest in their place; and corresponding to YHVH, which was within, "another god" rules; and corresponding to Shaddai, on the outside, its deadly poison rules in the flesh. Therefore both must be corrected: through poverty, since poverty is great — "how many bites of poverty bite him" — through this the bones too are broken, as though death ruled over them, and through this everything is corrected. And he said that poverty is like death and like the affliction of a metzora, as explained there. Thus we find poverty to be an atonement for this sin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:78: He also explains at the end of the statement that Torah is the remedy for all afflictions and all illnesses of the soul, as in "it shall be healing to your navel" — and this is if he has returned in repentance and does not return to his sin again.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:79: It is likewise understood from the whole of his words that blemishing the covenant causes poverty of money and poverty of Torah — the reason being that since the secret of the covenant is the secret of the river that flows and issues forth, it draws all kinds of flow, whether physical flow for the nourishment of the body or spiritual nourishment for the nourishment of souls; and since he has blemished it, both depart, and once he returns in repentance, both return. This is what is meant by "and if he returns in repentance, the elixir of life descends upon him, which is the Shechinah," and "heals him" from the poverty of Torah — for once the covenant is corrected, he has an ascent to attach himself to the Tree of Life, which is the middle pillar, the place from which Torah flows.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:80: The measure of the wording is thus: "and there is no poverty like the poverty of Torah" — meaning, as we have said above, that whoever blemishes the covenant is pursued by poverty such that he is considered as dead; there is no poverty like the poverty of Torah, and he is considered as dead even if he is wealthy. His remedy is to return in repentance, not to return to his sin, and to occupy himself with Torah so that it be a balm for his affliction, for by his ascending above the place of the blemish, he brings the elixir of life to heal the blemish placed there in the covenant, which is called "living."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:81: My teacher, peace be upon him, wrote that the elixir of Torah helps only after repentance, which is the abandonment of the sin, and the acceptance afterward of sufferings with love. The reason is that Torah is the elixir of life to purify the kelipah on the inside, while the sufferings purify the flesh from the outside, as explained above, that "another god" rests in the place of YHVH within, and the deadly poison rests in the place of Shaddai without.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:82: Nevertheless, it seems to my humble opinion, when we examine his words "and she is the healing for all illnesses, as in 'it shall be healing to your navel'" — that the intent is that Torah is a remedy both for what is outside, namely the flesh, and for what is inside, namely the bones — this being "healing to your navel," the flesh, and "drink for your bones," that is, the rest of the phrase, to be precise about the completion of the verse, which is needed for his intent. The reason is that Torah is like a poultice for a wound — after the bad flesh has been consumed, one applies a compress and poultice to grow good flesh; so the sufferings purify the kelipah both inside and outside, and this poor man remains afflicted, emaciated, his bones shrunk, and therefore he needs the elixir of Torah, which is a drink for the bones to moisten them, and a poultice for the flesh outside — this is "healing to your navel and drink for your bones." This is similar to what is explained in the Zohar (portion Vayakhel, 211b) regarding (Malachi 3:20), "and the sun of righteousness shall rise for you who fear My Name" etc., which is explained in the Gate of Awe, end of chapter 13.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:83: Also included in the repentance for this sin is being careful to guard the sign of Shabbat, the sign of tefillin, and the sign of the festivals. This is explained in Tikkunim (95a), these are their words: these are the supernal heh, the lower heh, the vav, the middle pillar, bearing both of them, the foundation of everything, yod — this is the covenant. Whoever uproots and deals falsely with it uproots everything and it falls; and this yod is the foundation stone from which the world was founded, of which it is said (Psalms 118:22), "the stone the builders rejected" etc., and it is the foundation of everything, upon which everything is built. Whoever sins against the sign of Shabbat, the sign of tefillin, the sign of the festivals, and the sign of the covenant of circumcision, is as though he uproots it from its place and returns the world to chaos and void. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:84: Since we find that Rashbi, peace be upon him, compared the sign of the covenant to the sign of Shabbat, the sign of tefillin, and the sign of the festival, it appears that the blemish is equal among them all, and one must be careful regarding all of them. And it is already known that our Sages of blessed memory said (Shabbat 118b) that whoever observes Shabbat according to its law, all his sins are forgiven, as it is said (Isaiah 56:2), "one who guards the Sabbath from profaning it [me'chalelo]" — do not read "me'chalelo" but "machul lo" ["he is forgiven"].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:85: Especially in the observance of the Sabbath day one must be very careful, since it resembles the sign of the covenant in many respects — and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, compared them, these are his words (Zohar, portion Yitro, beginning of 92): "remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy" (Exodus 20:8) — this is the secret of the holy covenant, for through this covenant all the sources of the body's limbs stand, and it includes everything; likewise Shabbat is the inclusion of the whole Torah, and all the secrets of Torah depend on it, and the establishment of Shabbat is the establishment of the whole Torah — for whoever guards Shabbat is as though he guards the whole Torah. Thus far his words.
